Title: ES|QL: Lookup on more flexible criteria than single exact match
Description:
**Value Proposition**

Lookup Join introduced the ability to do SQL-style LEFT OUTER JOINs in ES|QL. The initial release of Lookup Join relies on a common field name between the left index (from the source command) and the right index (the lookup index), and an exact match of the field values. This satisfies many use cases but more flexibility is needed for other use cases. Users need to match on multiple fields, more complex criteria like < or >, combine multiple criteria with AND and OR logic, and even full text function matching.

**Expected outcome**

ES|QL joins can satisfy a broader set of use cases by offering more expressive join predicates such as <, >, !=, multi-field matches, AND and OR logic, and  full text function matching. This can also reduce the need for altering the data schema or using workarounds like renaming and concatentation.

Title: Remove limitations on full text functions in ES|QL
Description:
**What the feature is**

Full text functions cannot be currently used in ES|QL after pipeline breakers or on runtime columns. We will lift both of these restrictions.

**Value proposition**

This change will reduce user friction and enable advanced search capabilities not available in query DSL via search on runtime columns. By allowing for full text functions after pipeline breakers, we enable actions like rescoring, and by allowing for search on runtime columns, users can go beyond keyword matching on these columns, but instead search on full text.

Example of a full text function after a pipeline breaker (`LIMIT`):

```
FROM books
| WHERE title:?query
| SORT title DESC
| LIMIT 100
| WHERE description:?query
```

Example of a full text function on a runtime column (syntax not finalized):

```
FROM books METDATA _score
| STATS languages = VALUES(language),
        titles = VALUES(title),
        rating = MAX(rating) BY code
| SORT rating DESC
| LIMIT 100
| WHERE match(titles, "Harry Potter")
        OR match(titles, "Harry Potter", { "index_analyzer": "my_analyzer"})
```

**Expected outcome**

Users can use full text functions after pipeline breakers or on runtime columns in ES|QL.

Title: ES|QL FORK command
Description:
**What the feature is**

The `FORK` processing command creates multiple execution branches to operate on the same input data and combines the results in a single output table.

In this quarter, we aim to move `FORK` from tech preview to GA.

**Value proposition**

Users can run multiple queries, differentiate, mutate, and merge them together. This can enable such search use cases such as [hybrid search with custom result fusion](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/hybrid-search-multi-stage-retrieval-esql), useful for cases where you need to bring in results from different indices or retrieval types.

```
FROM books METADATA _score, _id, _index
| FORK (WHERE KNN(description_vector, ?query_vector) | SORT _score DESC | LIMIT 100)
       (WHERE MATCH(description, ?query) | SORT _score DESC | LIMIT 100)
| FUSE // uses RRF by default
| SORT _score DESC
```

**Expected outcome**

We plan to make this General Availability.

Title: Streams: AI-Powered Log Ingestion and Analysis
Description:
**Value proposition**

Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) currently struggle with log data that is too noisy, expensive, and unstructured to serve as a primary signal for troubleshooting. Streams addresses this by using AI to transform raw logs into actionable intelligence, automating the heavy lifting of data partitioning, parsing, and retention management. This empowers teams to pinpoint the root cause of issues immediately and reduces the operational complexity of maintaining custom ingestion pipelines.

Most capabilities are expected to be available for regular data streams as well, while some will be reserved for the new /logs experience, as they would cause breaking changes otherwise.

**Expected outcome**
Ingest raw logs in any format (structured or unstructured) from any source directly into Elasticsearch without the need for specific agents or complex pipeline configurations.

Utilize AI-driven partitioning to automatically segment incoming log streams into distinct components, such as services or systems.

Apply AI-based parsing to automatically detect log structures and generate GROK rules, eliminating manual schema management.

Surface "Significant Events" such as startup messages, out-of-memory errors, and anomalies to provide a prioritized starting point for investigations.

Enable data quality management through a failure store that captures and exposes failed documents for inspection and fix.

**Optional: Key user stories / use cases**

Title: Improved Search and Filtering for the Case List
Description:
This feature improves the search and filtering capabilities on the Case list page. It will expand the quick search to include more relevant case data beyond just the title and description, such as text from comments. This update will also introduce a time-range filter, allowing users to find cases created within specific timeframes (e.g., "last 7 days" or an absolute date range).

**Value proposition**
Currently, analysts can find it difficult to locate specific cases, as the search is limited and time-based filtering is not available. This forces users to rely on manual searching or inefficient workarounds. By expanding search and adding a time filter, the goal is to decrease the time it takes for analysts to find the exact case they are looking for.

**Expected outcome**
After this update, users will be able to perform the following new actions:

- Quickly find cases by searching or filtering for key terms, indicators, or other data (like an IP address, a keyword from a comment, an alert ID, etc.) directly from the Case list page.
- Easily filter the Case list to show only cases created within a specific time range (e.g., "last 24 hours" or "all of October 2025").

Title: More Advanced Insights for Increased Correlations
Description:
## More Advanced Insights for Increased Correlations

### Value proposition

To enhance the alert and attack investigation experience, we will evolve our capabilities to provide more advanced insights for correlating related information. This includes cross-referencing information such as related cases and alerts, as well as related attacks, entities, and chats. By correlating with other critical content, this expanded context will help users prioritize their investigations effectively.

### Expected outcome

As a user triaging and investigating suspicious activity, it is critical to understand related information. This can be related alerts, attacks, entities, or even previous investigations or chats. All of this information can help add context to the current investigation and potentially help prioritize the activity for response or further investigation.

Title: User Defined Alert Templates
Description:
## User Defined Alert Templates

### Value proposition

Users currently spend time customizing their alert experience for different use cases by adjusting page controls, visualizations, table columns, and event table grouping. However, these configurations are only saved locally, which prevents sharing them with team members.

This feature will solve this limitation by allowing users to save their customized alert configurations as shareable templates. The capability may also be expanded beyond the alerts page in the future. By enabling teams to create and share these templates, we will ensure curated and consistent experiences for responding to various types of events.

### Expected outcome

Users need greater flexibility and personalization within their Security Solution experience, particularly on the alerts page. Given the wide range of alert types—from authentication events to network, endpoint, and cloud—and the varying detection methods (e.g. machine learning, aggregations, threat match, etc.), users require the ability to tailor their view. They will achieve this by customizing the default table configuration, applying specific filters and controls, and modifying table grouping. Once these personalized views are created, users will have the ability to save and share them with their teams.

Title: Release of Improved Attack Experience
Description:
## Release of Improved Attack Experience

### Value proposition

The focus of this initiative is the general availability (GA) release of the enhanced attack experience. To effectively triage attacks, analysts need consistency with the existing alert workflows, as previously discussed. Key improvements include better alert correlations, improved table grouping functionality, and new attack viewers to facilitate context pivoting.

### Expected outcome

Users expect a supported, GA set of features for triaging and investigating attacks. This will include improved experiences for responding to attacks.

Title: New Detection Overview Dashboard
Description:
## New Detection Overview Dashboard

### Value proposition

As experiences evolve to improve the triage of attacks and alerts, users require a clear detections overview dashboard within the Security Solution. This dashboard will summarize critical detections and provide users with key performance indicators (KPIs) related to all alert and attack data.

Key features may include:
* **Alert and Attack Metrics**: Summaries of critical alerts, including team assignment breakdowns, alert severity, and response times.
* **False Positive Analysis**: Utilization of the new alert close reason feature to incorporate metrics on why detections are being closed, such as tracking false positive rates and their improvement over time.
* **Comparative Analytics**: Core functionality focused on time-based comparisons, enabling teams to understand if they are experiencing a higher impact from alerts today than previously.
* **AI-Powered Guidance**: Integration of generative AI to provide summarized context and actionable guidance on the next steps for users.

### Expected outcome

Create a single, central dashboard for Security Operations Center (SOC) leads and teams to monitor and understand their alert and attack response performance. This should provide a summarized view for a quick, high-level summary of response effectiveness. There should be the presence of standard metrics to track and display critical performance indicators such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Respond (MTTR). Trend analysis should show performance trends over time to facilitate continuous improvement and content needs to be actionable so users can pivot from the dashboard to relevant, detailed content for deeper investigation.

Title: New Attack Viewer for Context Pivoting
Description:
## New Attack Viewer for Context Pivoting

### Value proposition

Analyst workflows currently include a dedicated experience for viewing attacks, which is effective for immediate response. However, this approach limits the ability to easily cross-reference and preview attack details within other relevant contexts. For example, when an analyst is viewing an alert associated with an attack, they are currently forced to navigate to a separate page.

To streamline this process, we plan to enable a more flexible workflow by introducing a dedicated attack view, similar to the existing alert view. This will allow users to preview attack information directly within their current context, eliminating the need to pivot between applications and facilitating a more integrated user experience.

### Expected outcome

When interacting with indexed data (documents or simply, rows in a table), users expect the ability to view the selected content in a separate, portable view while keeping the primary data table accessible.

Similar to the established alert experience, where alerts are managed and viewed on a dedicated page, users expect a consistent interaction pattern for attacks, which are stored in the same manner. This expectation extends beyond merely viewing attacks like alerts; users also need to reference attacks from various other contexts, including alerts, events, entities, and cases.

Title: Improved Attack Triage Experience
Description:
## Improved Attack Triage Experience

### Value proposition

Attack Discovery provides analysts with a summarized detection that groups and contextualizes related alerts. With the release of attack scheduling, analysts require a dedicated experience for triage and response. By basing this on the familiar alerts page, analysts will have established workflows for responding to and investigating the content of attacks, particularly the associated alerts.

### Expected outcome
Users viewing attack details must be able to search, filter, and group the associated content. Beyond the attack information itself, the most critical content is the details contained within the associated alerts.

The new experience will provide users full access to all linked alerts and the ability to freely search this content to identify significant attacks. Furthermore, users should be able to benefit from attack content during traditional alert triage. It must be simple to prioritize alerts based on whether they are associated with an attack or are standalone.

Title: Alert Close with Reason
Description:
# **Alert Close with Reason**

## **Value proposition**

To streamline the alert triage process, we will enhance the alert closure workflow. Currently, analysts complete their investigation or response by closing an alert and can optionally add tags or notes to document their findings. While helpful, this existing method is not a streamlined solution.

By requiring analysts to select a "reason" when closing an alert, we can capture critical metrics to improve team performance and operations. For example, consistently tracking "false positive" as a close reason allows the detection engineering team to directly identify and refine problematic detection rules. This standardized approach ensures that valuable information about the alert's disposition is systematically stored.

## **Expected outcome**

Users require the ability to close an alert and provide a summary reason for the closure. Initially, these reasons will not be customizable, but users will expect customization, similar to the existing alert tagging workflow. The process of defining a close reason must also be accessible via APIs to support automation workflows. This reason will be stored in a dedicated field within the alert document, specifically `kibana.alert.workflow_reason`. While this added information allows users to create custom visualizations, the goal is to enhance default experiences in the future.

Title: Add Windows ARM support for Elastic Defend
Description:
**What the feature is (as Title)**: Windows ARM support for Elastic Defend

**Value proposition**: With native ARM support, analysts can monitor and protect all Windows endpoints with the same fidelity, speed, and reliability as traditional x86 systems.

Adding Elastic Defend support for ARM eliminates coverage gaps as organizations adopt ARM-based laptops and Copilot+ PCs, ensuring that detections, response actions, and investigations work consistently across the entire fleet. The lightweight ARM agent delivers lower CPU impact, faster event collection, and seamless integration with Elastic Security’s existing rules, dashboards, and response workflows.

**Expected outcome**:Customers expect architecture transparency and support parity, offering Windows ARM support for Elastic Defend removes friction in endpoint deployments, specifically  for large and diverse device fleets.

Title: Custom YARA rules
Description:
**Value proposition**
Enable Elastic Defend users to automatically detect known malware and suspicious patterns through automated YARA scans integrated with Elastic Defend, while also providing the flexibility to add and manage custom YARA rules directly from the Elastic Security UI. This enhances Elastic Defend’s threat detection depth and gives analysts more control over custom detection logic without relying on external tools.

**Expected outcome**
- Elastic Defend will automatically execute YARA scans.
- Analysts can create, import, and manage custom YARA rules within Elastic Security.
- Scan detections are promoted as detection alerts, enabling better investigation and correlation workflows in Security Investigations and Timeline.
- Improves detection coverage against commodity and advanced threats, and supports threat hunting use cases aligned with malware research workflows.

**Key user stories / use cases**
- As an analyst, I can define custom YARA rules within Elastic Security so I can detect specific malware families relevant to my environment.
- As an incident responder, I can view YARA detections directly from detections alerts, correlating detected matches with Elastic Defend telemetry for deeper analysis.
- As an administrator, I can centrally manage and distribute custom YARA rules across my organization through Elastic Agent policy configurations.

Title: Endpoint Forensics - Osquery
Description:
**Value proposition**
Enable analysts and responders to perform deep forensic analysis directly from Elastic Security Osquery Manager by enhancing osquery-based endpoint visibility, performance, and usability. This includes expanding forensic coverage via new osquery tables (browser history, amcache, jumplists and open handles and improving the in-product osquery interface with new out-of-the-box queries and packs to streamline investigative workflows.

**Expected outcome**
Elastic Security users can run faster and more intuitive forensic queries through a redesigned osquery UI, benefiting from improved performance, richer data, and reduced query complexity. Analysts will be able to access critical forensic artifacts without switching tools, accelerating triage and investigation within the Elastic platform.

**Key user stories / use cases**

- As an incident responder, I want to query forensic artifacts like Amcache or browser history from the Elastic UI to determine process execution sources.
- As a forensic analyst, I want prebuilt queries for common artifacts so I can focus on analysis rather than syntax.
- As a SOC investigator, I want faster and more reliable osquery execution across large environments to support time-sensitive incident response.
- As a threat hunter, I want to pivot from an alert to forensic context directly, without needing external forensic tools.

Title: Memory dump Linux response action
Description:
**Value proposition**
Extend Elastic Security’s forensic and response capabilities to Linux endpoints by enabling remote process memory dump collection. This allows analysts to capture memory snapshots from specific Linux processes directly from the Response Console, facilitating rapid malware triage, memory-resident threat detection, and post-compromise investigation.

**Expected outcome**

- Introduce a new process dump response action for Linux endpoints.
- Support dumping a specific process’s memory.
- Collected dumps are transferred and stored securely within Elastic for further export (downloadable DMP file).

**Key user stories / use cases**

- As a SOC analyst, I want to capture a dump of a suspicious Linux process so I can analyze its memory for injected code or malicious payloads.
- As a forensic analyst, I want to correlate process dumps with related alerts or sessions to confirm in-memory malware behavior.

Title: Browser history and amcache osquery tables
Description:
**Value proposition**
Add two osquery extension tables  to Elastic’s osquery offering: browser_history (for major browsers: Chrome, Edge/Chromium, Firefox, Safari where applicable) and amcache (Windows Amcache.hve parsing). These extensions give investigators and hunters immediate, normalized access to browser navigation artifacts and executed-program history directly from Elastic-managed osquery agents. This improves triage speed, enriches detections, and reduces time-to-evidence collection inside Elastic Security.  ￼

**Expected outcome**
- Analysts can run live queries and scheduled packs over browser history and Amcache across hosts via Osquery Manager in Kibana.  ￼
- Data is normalized to ECS fields where possible (URL, timestamp, user, host, file path, file hash) enabling seamless correlation with other telemetry.

Title: Windows Memory Dump response action
Description:
**Value proposition**
Enable Elastic Security users to remotely collect memory dumps from Windows endpoints directly through the response console, improving investigation and incident response workflows. This feature empowers analysts to perform advanced forensic analysis on volatile memory artifacts, such as injected processes, credential theft, or fileless malware.

**Expected outcome**

- Analysts can initiate a kernel or process-specific memory dump from the Elastic Security Response Console.
- The dump file is securely transferred and stored in Elastic as downloadable artifact.
- Dump file will be in `.DMP` format allowing integration with memory analysis tools (e.g., Volatility).

**Key user stories / use cases**

- As a SOC analyst, I want to remotely collect a memory dump from a Windows host so I can analyze potential in-memory threats without requiring additional tooling.
- As a forensic investigator, I want to selectively dump a suspicious process to identify injected code or hidden threads.

Title: FedRAMP High Authorization for Elastic Cloud Hosted on AWS GovCloud
Description:
**What the feature is**
We are working toward achieving FedRAMP High authorization for our Elastic Cloud Hosted (ECH) product in AWS GovCloud (US). This authorization would certify that Elastic’s managed cloud platform satisfies more than 400 rigorous FedRAMP controls, ensuring secure and compliant operations for mission-critical workloads across federal, state, and local agencies. For organizations responsible for managing and protecting highly sensitive data—such as those in law enforcement, emergency response, healthcare, and financial systems—Elastic Cloud Hosted at FedRAMP High will enable agencies to deploy Elastic’s full suite of search, observability, and security capabilities in a fully authorized, government-compliant cloud environment. This allows public sector customers to achieve faster threat detection, gain AI-driven insights, and maintain compliance with strict federal mandates.

**Expected outcome**
Public sector customers will be able to confidently leverage Elastic Cloud Hosted with FedRAMP High authorization, empowering agencies to modernize IT operations, strengthen cybersecurity resilience, and improve operational efficiency—all within a FedRAMP High-authorized, scalable, and cost-effective cloud solution.

Title: Best-Practice OOTB Alerts for popular off-the-shelf services with Elastic Integrations
Description:
**What the feature is (as Title)** Best-Practice OOTB Alerts for popular off-the-shelf services with Elastic Integrations
Elastic OOTB alert rule templates enable users to set monitoring coverage for their most popular off the shelf services, with minimum investment and expertise needed. 

**Value proposition**
***- User & Problem:***
SREs and developers who rely on critical Elastic-monitored services (e.g., AWS S3, NGINX, PostgreSQL) face significant time sink and risk when setting up monitoring for them. They must invest considerable time researching, configuring, and manually maintaining bespoke alert rules, often missing critical signals or violating service-level objectives (SLOs) due to the scattered and non-standardized nature of "best practice" documentation.

***- Proposed Solution:***
Elastic Curated Best-Practice Alert Templates for Integrations. This feature embeds expert knowledge directly into the platform, providing pre-configured, production-ready alert rule templates for key signals across popular off-the-shelf services (e.g., AWS S3, NGINX, PostgreSQL). The templates are automatically deployed and updated as the underlying Elastic Integration evolves.:***

**Expected outcome**
***- Key Benefits & Value:***

Eliminate Alert Research: Instantly create alerts for critical signals (e.g., NGINX 5xx errors, high PostgreSQL query latency, AWS S3 throttling) with minimal research time.

**Accelerate Time-to-Value:** Move from deploying an Integration to having full, production-grade alerting coverage in minutes, not days.

**Guaranteed Relevance:** Alert templates are maintained by Elastic, ensuring template rules are automatically updated to match new service versions, telemetry changes, or evolving best practices. Users will be able to easily update rules when templates change, with minimal effort.

**Reduce MTTD:** Enable early visibility into critical threshold breaches, allowing teams to solve operational issues before they escalate into high-severity outages. 

***- Key jobs-to-be-done:***
This capability enables customers to solve the following customer goals, questions and problems:
1. What are the recommended alerts for the services I'm monitoring with the integrations (eg AWS S3, NGINX, PostgreSQL, etc)?
2. What are the recommended configurations?
3. Why are you recommending them?
4. Some rule threshold and other config are context specific (for example, CPU utilization). What guidelines should I use to tweak the thresholds?
5. …

Title: Enhanced Insight and Usability of OOTB Dashboards for popular off-the-shelf services
Description:
**What the feature is (as Title)** Enhanced Insight and Usability of OOTB Dashboards for popular off-the-shelf services
We are reimagining the OOTB dashboards for popular off-the-shelf (OTS) services, to deliver enhanced insight and a superior user experience. Our focus is on better usability, navigability, structure based on key use cases, and visual consistency. This ensures users can quickly answer their most frequent questions, understand service health, and effortlessly troubleshoot operational issues by seeing the most important data upfront.

**Value proposition**
We will provide SREs and developers using OTS services with a superior, purpose-built OOTB dashboard experience that turns complex operational data into immediate, actionable insight, allowing them to troubleshoot faster and manage service health with confidence. 

**Expected outcome**

1. Task-Oriented Navigation and Discovery
Users will be able to easily find information depending on the task at hand. The dashboards will be organized around common use cases and component-centric views, dramatically reducing search time and cognitive load.

2. Effortless Troubleshooting with Context
Users will be able to follow a clear path to resolution using contextual navigation. They will be able to find related information with intuitive drill-downs that move logically from high-level summaries (like overall service health) to granular details (like specific sub-components) without losing context.

3. Rapid Data Filtering and Focus
Improved usability of filters to necessary data only with smart, context-aware filters. This enables users to instantly focus on specific namespaces, workloads, or timeframes, accelerating analysis and bypassing data clutter.

4. Confident Operational Decisions
Ultimately, this combination of structure, clarity, and rapid access to information ensures users can quickly and accurately answer their most frequent questions. This leads to greater confidence in managing service health and effortless troubleshooting of operational issues.

Title: [LLM Observability] Amazon Bedrock AgentCore observability
Description:
**What the feature is (as Title)**  [LLM Observability] Observability for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

**Value proposition**
Developers and SREs who run agentic workloads on Bedrock AgentCore want to be able to understand the performance, reliability, cost and output quality. This enables them to monitor the health of their agentic workloads and have the necessary observability for quicker root cause analysis during operational issues. AI agentic applications leverage complex workflows between LLMs, agents and tools. LLMs are opaque and non-determining systems which could have unpredictable output, cost and performance spikes. Users need an evolved layer on top of traditional observability to be able to address these needs.

Elastic LLM Observability for agentic AI applications enables users to observe the AgentCore platform in which their workloads run, as well as get detailed information on the execution path of their applications for easy troubleshooting. They get curated set of metrics and logs with pre-configured out of the box dashboards. To enable root cause analysis, Elastic APM visualizes the flow of execution with information such as tokens, latency, LLMs, agents, tool calls, etc. 

**Expected outcome**
- Integration with  AWS to get vended AWS metrics and logs for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
- Out of the box dashboards (as part of the integration) for the vended metrics and logs
- OTel-native APM traces for AI agentic apps running in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Title: Late Chunking support for JinaAI embeddings
Description:
## Value proposition

Enable higher-relevance retrieval on long documents by adding Late Chunking support for JinaAI embeddings to the Inference API. Unlike naïve chunking -which splits first, embeds each chunk, then pools- Late Chunking embeds the full document first and then chunks based on the embedded tokens.

This ordering preserves significantly more cross-chunk context, improving semantic continuity and reducing "lost signal". The result is measurable relevance gains on long-form content, especially for documents in the 1,500+ token range, where standard chunking may degrade search quality.

## Expected outcome  

Inference API Late Chunking support for JinaAI embeddings.

Description:

With Elastic’s Inference API you ship AI faster, without lock-in. It integrates an array of models for embeddings, reranking, chat completions, and powers full RAG pipelines with a unified, intuitive Elasticsearch query across leading model providers. We handle the provider-specific complexity and orchestration, giving you one seamless syntax to access leading models and inference infrastructures.

## Expected outcome  

We are adding the following integrations for the Chat Completions GenAI task to the Inference API:

## Value proposition

Turn noisy logs to signal, fast. Use ES|QL-powered Log Pattern Analysis in your Discover workflows to cluster messages, surface what changed, and drill into root causes, all without context switching or hopping tools, drastically speeding RCA and reducing MTTR.

Description:
## Value proposition

Get near-instant insights from massive datasets by executing high-speed, approximate analytical queries. This allows them to make faster analysis in Discover and Dashboards without waiting for resource-intensive, exact computations.

- A range (confidence interval)

Description:
## Value proposition

By integrating Anomaly Detection job and datafeed management into the Elasticsearch Terraform provider, we transform what can be a slow, complex, error-prone, and manual process into an automated, auditable, and scalable "as code" workflow.

Operational bottlenecks are eliminated and organizations are empowered to rapidly deploy, update, and govern their monitoring capabilities at scale. This can also reduce the dependency on "centers of excellence" or teams of experts and it powers easy adoption across hundreds of teams and thousands of microservices. 

## Expected outcome  

- Support for the `anomaly_detectors` API
- Support for the `datafeeds` API

### User pain points addressed

**1. Lack of scalability and lifecycle automation for the enterprise**
> _"Any user should be able to say: Here’s a new microservice, I can create an AD job for it, easily and automatically"._ 
-Wells Fargo 

**2. Operational bottlenecks and lack of self-service**
> _"It is not realistic to use it at enterprise scale with hundreds of teams"._ 
-Wells Fargo

**3. Lack of version control and auditability**

Title: Integrated Multi-Modal Search: Generate and Search Image Vectors Directly in Elasticsearch
Description:
## Value proposition

By integrating multimodal models into the Inference API, we are changing what "search" means for a developer using Elastic. For the first time, developers can generate multi-modal vectors within Elastic for applications that perform sophisticated multi-modal search, like searching images with text, by using the same single, seamless and intuitive Elasticsearch Inference API syntax they already know. 

This integration allows developers to build, deploy, and scale applications that can see, read, and understand complex, real-world information in Elastic, rather than having to bring their image and multi-modal vectors from external platforms.

## Expected outcome  

MVP to generate multi-modal vectors (text and image) in Elastic to enable multi-modal search.

**Example use cases:**

- E-commerce: An online fashion retailer allows customers to search through clothing and accessories using natural language queries. It recommends items based on visual similarity (image-to-image) alongside similarity based on natural language descriptions and positive reviews by customers with similar profiles.
- RAG for customer and technical support: A manufacturer has thousands of technical documents and manuals involving: text and technical diagrams with functional and technical descriptions and operational instructions. Customers or technicians can ask questions or for troubleshooting steps and the response may contain instructions with diagrams.
- An AI search engine for researchers has thousands of research publications. Researchers describe a topic in natural language and the tool returns an overview, retrieving the most relevant articles and understanding charts, text and tables.

Title: Improved datetime picker for faster incident response and data analysis
Description:
**What the feature is**
An overhaul of the Kibana datetime range selector (in Discover, Dashboards, etc.) to help users be more efficient in troubleshooting observability and security incidents. 

**Value Proposition**
The improved timepicker reduces the time spent configuring a time range and accelerates incident response and data exploration. By allowing users to save and share time range presets and offering easy copy/paste functionality, it establishes a consistent and rapid workflow across multiple analysis tabs. Clearly surfacing the active timezone prevents configuration errors and ensures accurate analysis for global teams, ultimately making Kibana more productive.

**Expected Outcome**
- Fast Selection & Presets: Single-click access for common relative ranges, plus the ability to save, name, and recall custom time range presets.
- Persist time range across tabs: Easy copy/paste of the active time range and timezone string between Kibana tabs/apps.
- Timezone visibility: The active timezone setting is prominently displayed within the component.

**Key User Stories / Use Cases**
User Story: "As a security analyst, I want to save my frequent 'Monday 8 AM to 9 AM' range as a preset to apply it instantly every week."
User Story: "As an analyst, I want to copy the complex 3-hour relative range I set in one dashboard and paste it immediately into another tab to ensure I’m comparing the exact same data."

Title: Browser locale language support in Kibana
Description:
**What the feature is**
Browser Locale Language allows users to view the Kibana interface in their preferred language (French, German, Japanese, Chinese, or English) by automatically detecting and applying the setting configured in their web browser, without having to configure a .yml file. 

**Value Proposition**
Currently, global organizations are forced to default all users to English, despite having employees across multiple countries and languages. Users on Serverless cannot change their language setting. This creates a significant usability gap and makes Kibana less accessible and less competitive compared to multi-language competitors like Grafana and Splunk. By automatically detecting the browser locale, Kibana offers a personalized experience that improves adoption may make it easier for some customers to migrate from on-premises to Elastic Cloud and Serverless.

**Expected Outcome**
- Kibana will automatically detect the user's browser-set preferred language on first load and apply the corresponding language (e.g., zh-CN, ja-JP, fr-FR).
- Users can override the language setting with a UI control
- For on-premise users, this UI setting will override the default language set in kibana.yml, enabling multi-language support even within a single on-prem deployment.

**Key User Stories / Use Cases**
User Story: "As a Japanese Analyst on Serverless, I want Kibana to automatically appear in Japanese when I log in, without having to ask my administrator to change a server configuration file I don't have access to."
User Story: "As a Global Administrator of an ECH deployment, I want users in Germany and France to be able to use Kibana in their respective languages without me having to manage separate deployment instances."

Title: Unified and Searchable Case Attachments
Description:
We are redesigning how evidence is managed in Cases. This update will replace the separate tabs for Alerts, Events, and Observables with a single, unified "Attachments" tab that consolidates all evidence into one scalable location.

**Value proposition**
In complex investigations, analysts may attach hundreds of pieces of evidence to a single case. Manually scrolling through long lists to find a specific item is slow and inefficient. This change will help to speed up investigations by making it easier or analysts to find the exact evidence they need, helping to lower Mean Time To Respond (MTTR).

**Expected outcome**

- View all attached evidence within a single, consolidated "Attachments" tab.
- See a summary of all attachment types included in the case (e.g., Alerts, Observables, Events).
- Filter within specific attachment types (like Alerts or Events) to find the evidence you need without manual scrolling.

Title: Draft Cases
Description:
Introduces a "Draft" state for cases, providing a dedicated space for initial triage and evidence collection before a formal incident is declared.

**Value proposition**
Decouples the act of investigating from the act of declaring an incident. This allows teams to safely separate "signal" from "noise," ensuring that low-confidence investigations do not pollute critical metrics like Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) or trigger unintended automated responses.

**Expected outcome**
Users will be able to create and collaborate on Draft cases to validate findings. These cases can be seamlessly promoted to standard Cases once a threat is verified, or closed without impacting performance stats. This distinction will be exposed in the data schema to support filtered reporting and smarter automation logic.

Title: Event Attachments for Cases

**Value proposition**
Improve investigative context by allowing analysts to attach any relevant event, providing a more complete and flexible evidence locker. This enables analysts to pinpoint and save suspicious events that may not have triggered a formal alert, ensuring all evidence can be captured in one place.

**Expected outcome**
Users will be able to attach individual events from various views within the Security Solution directly to a new or existing Case.

**Value proposition**
This update accelerates the triage and investigation process by eliminating manual data entry. This automation helps analysts save time, reduce errors, and more quickly correlate related activities. 

**Expected outcome**
When enabled, analysts will find that relevant observables from their alerts are automatically populated within the Case, and the Similar Cases tab is populated based on the attached observables.

**Value proposition**
Enable security analysts to conduct faster and more accurate threat hunts by providing them with the complete historical context and relationship mapping for entity and behavioral changes.

Title: AI-Driven Entity Analytics
Description:
**Background:**

Entity Analytics represent the key pieces of information involved in a security incident in a SIEM. They are the “who”, “what”, “where”, and “when” of any research, hunt or investigation providing crucial context for effective response. Entities are objects in every modern SIEM and can include users, hosts, files, network artifacts, threat intelligence, vulnerabilities and much more.

Threat hunting has traditionally been a highly manual process requiring deep expertise in adversary behaviors, query languages, infrastructure, users and security analysis. Most organizations lack dedicated threat hunters or the time required to perform regular hunting operations. Even when orgs have the resources, the process is inefficient and often reactive rather than proactive.

**What problem are we solving**

Among the personas that comprise our customers' security operations teams, many of them rely on complex processes and query languages in order to investigate and find threats and risky behaviors in their environments. Threat hunting activities, in particular, are in need of this specialized, technical knowledge on a regular basis, as these individuals who go hunting are proactive.

We can significantly impact and streamline threat hunting activities through natural language, by providing guided experiences based on the combination of generative AI, entity analytics data, curated threat intelligence, and the powerful search analytics capabilities provided by Elastic.

**Expected outcome**

Deliver AI-driven entity analytics, including historical entity store, NL-driven entity queries, entity resolution, NL-based visualizations, and more, to satisfy today’s SIEM requirement that was historically fulfilled by legacy UEBA vendors, to complement all analyst and threat hunting workflows, as well as the needs of insider threat teams.

**Roadmaps Included**
- Privilege User Monitoring
- Entity Risk Scoring Alert Filtering

- Historical Context Changes & Behavioral Baseline

- Overview Homepage
- Entity Graph

Title: Query Streams and Draft Mode
Description:
### Value proposition:

Users need more flexibility in how they organize, view, and process their data. Sometimes they need to create custom, reusable views that span multiple data sources (e.g., "all production errors"), or filter a single source. 

Other times, they need to safely test new ingest-time processing and partitioning rules without risking production data. This feature introduces two powerful capabilities: 
- Query Streams let users define new virtual, read-only streams using ES|QL
- Draft Mode provides a way to test and preview new ingest logic at query-time before making it permanent.

### Expected behaviors:

This feature is composed of two related functionalities:

**1. Query Streams (Virtual Data Views)**
* Define and create a new, queryable stream using a free-form **ES|QL query**.
* Create "standalone" streams to unify data from multiple sources (e.g., `FROM logs.nginx, logs.k8s.nginx*`).
* Create "sub-streams" to create a filtered, read-only view of an existing stream (e.g., `FROM my_stream WHERE status_code > 400`).
* These streams are **virtual and read-only**; they do not store data and resolve the query at read time.
* Attach assets like dashboards and alerts directly to these virtual streams once available in Streams (outside of this initial feature).

**2. Draft Mode (Safe Processing Testing)**
* Create new Log Sub Streams in a new **"Draft Mode."**
* Define partitioning and processing rules in this safe "sandbox" environment.
* This logic is **applied at query time**, not at ingest time, allowing you to preview the results on live data without any permanent impact.
* Validate your new processing logic (e.g., in dashboards) to ensure it's correct.
* Once confident, **"Promote"** the draft rules to make them permanent, which applies them to the live ingest pipeline.

Title: Logs Streams
Description:
### Value proposition:

Observability, security, and platform engineers need a simple, consistent, and scalable way to manage their log data. Today, this often requires manually configuring and maintaining complex index templates, ingest pipelines, and retention policies across many disparate data sources, which is error-prone and time-consuming. 

Logs Streams provide an opinionated, managed, and hierarchical system for all logs. This allows users to easily organize data (e.g., `logs` $\to$ `logs.production` $\to$ `logs.production.api`), with settings like processing, schema, and retention being automatically inherited by sub-streams. This dramatically simplifies configuration, ensures consistency, and provides a single, queryable entity for all your log data.

### Expected behaviors:

* **Hierarchical Organization:** Organize all logs under a single, high-level `logs` stream and create "Ingest Sub Streams" (e.g., `logs.production.api`) to partition data.
* **Setting Inheritance:** Define ingest processing, mappings, and retention policies on a parent stream (e.g., `logs.production`), and all its sub-streams will automatically inherit these settings.
* **Automatic Normalization:** Incoming log data is automatically processed and normalized to an OTel-like shape, ensuring consistent field names and types out-of-the-box.
* **Centralized Management:** Manage the full lifecycle of your logs. From ingest processing to schema and retention, in one place.

Title: Intelligent Asset Suggestions and AI Generation
Description:
### Value proposition:

When users add data to a stream, they often face a "blank slate" problem, requiring manual effort to build relevant dashboards, processing rules, and alerts. This feature provides an AI-powered assistant to solve this. It will proactively analyze data and make deterministic suggestions from a knowledge base (e.g., "This looks like Nginx data, apply this dashboard?"). Furthermore, it will introduce generative AI workflows to create new assets, either based on the system's understanding of the data or by allowing users to ask for new content in natural language. This dramatically accelerates time-to-value, helping all users get insights from their data immediately.

### Expected behaviors:

* **Deterministic Suggestions:** Automatically analyze data sent to a stream and suggest relevant, pre-built assets (like processing logic, dashboards, or alert rules) from an Elastic knowledge base.
* **Proactive AI Generation:** Proactively generate new, suggested assets (like a starter dashboard) based on the system's automated understanding of the data's structure and content.
* **Reactive AI Generation:** Provide generative AI workflows that allow users to create new assets (like visualizations or processing rules) using natural language prompts.
* All generative AI features will be clearly marked as "Preview."

### Key user stories / use cases:

* **As an SRE,** when I send new AWS logs to a stream, the system recognizes the data and suggests, "We recommend applying the standard AWS S3 dashboard and processing rules."
* **As an engineer,** I send custom application logs to a new stream. The system analyzes the fields and proactively generates a "starter" dashboard showing a timeline of events and a table of the most common fields.
* **As an analyst,** I am viewing a stream and I use a prompt to ask the AI, "Build a pie chart showing the distribution of `http.status_code` and a bar chart of the top 10 `user.name`."

Title: Improved AI Suggestions for Stream Partitioning and Processing
Description:
### What the feature is

Improved AI Suggestions for Stream Partitioning and Processing

---

### Value proposition

Users onboarding new data often struggle with the manual effort required to partition streams and define complex processing rules like Grok patterns. Existing AI suggestions help, but can be overly specific, don't cover the full pipeline (like date parsing), or are inflexible, forcing users to make manual corrections after accepting. This initiative will enhance our AI capabilities to provide more flexible and comprehensive assistance. Users will benefit from smarter, more generalized Grok and Dissect patterns, suggestions for entire multi-step ingest pipelines, and the ability to review and refine all AI-generated suggestions before saving them.

---

### Expected behaviors

* Provide AI-generated suggestions for `dissect` processors, in addition to existing `grok` suggestions.
* Improve AI-generated `grok` patterns to be more general and less overly specific (e.g., by better handling whitespace and generic data fields).
* Suggest entire multi-step processing pipelines (e.g., Grok + Date + Remove processors) rather than just a single processor.
* Allow users to review, edit (e.g., change the name or condition), and refine AI-generated partition suggestions before accepting them.

---

### Key user stories / use cases

* As a user, when my log message contains a custom timestamp, I want the AI to suggest not only the `grok` pattern to extract it, but also the `date` processor needed to parse it and set it as the `@timestamp`.
* As a user, when my logs have minor variations, I want the AI to generate a `grok` pattern that is general enough to handle all variations, rather than a brittle pattern that only matches a few samples.
* As a user, when my data is delimited (like CSV or space-delimited), I want the AI to suggest a `dissect` pattern to parse it.
* As a user, when the AI suggests a partition named `logs.trader-logs`, I want to edit the name to `logs.trader` before I accept the suggestion.

Title: Improved memory monitoring for vector use cases
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**

Aside from monitoring the Elasticsearch JVM heap memory, AutoOps now monitors the system (i.e. so-called off-heap) memory in order to ensure that users relying on hybrid and semantic search get notified proactively before experiencing performance degradations when searching through vector data.

**Value proposition**

Users' confidence on hybrid and semantic search will increase as they will literally benefit from a safety net when searching through vector data by getting advanced notice from AutoOps with recommendations on how to improve their memory consumption and prevent search performance from degrading.

Title: Open API for AutoOps data
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**

AutoOps now offers a way to retrieve insights and recommendations through an open API, which unlocks many new opportunities for all users eager to get access to AutoOps data in a programmatic way.

**Value proposition**

AutoOps-derived intelligence and insights are now available for users to build upon. Exported AutoOps data can now be consumed in a number of different ways, e.g. to create tools for an MCP server, as an input for the new Workflow engine, or simply to be exported into another data store and enrich it.

Title: Information about slow ES|QL queries is available in AutoOps
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**

As part of detecting and surfacing long-running search tasks, AutoOps performs an analysis of the underlying DSL or ES|QL search query, and provides a list of potential reasons for increased latency. This feature is useful to any kind of users who want to leverage the new ES|QL query language for their search, observability or security use cases, and especially to security engineers who rely on ES|QL-based detection rules that need to run on very big data sets.

**Value proposition**

Customers' confidence to leverage ES|QL will increase as they will get specific insights into why their queries can be slow running, where these queries are originating from and gain a better understanding on how to craft more performant ones.

Title: Serverless monitoring with AutoOps - EIS Tier
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**
The EIS Tier view in AutoOps for Elastic Cloud Serverless provides visibility into how inference performance, and token usage, helping users understand how inference activities impact overall project efficiency and usage.

This capability is designed for Serverless users running inference workloads who want to track their token consumption, optimize performance, and manage costs more effectively.

**Value proposition**
The EIS Tier view links EIS performance metrics with inference billing dimensions, showing how inference workloads drive token usage. It helps users monitor token consumption, identify resource-intensive models, and adjust configurations to improve efficiency.

Together with the Search, Search AI Lake, and Indexing Tier views, it gives users deeper visibility into how different workload types contribute to overall Serverless resource usage and costs—supporting data-driven optimization and cost control.

Title: Elastic Inference Service (EIS) for Self Managed Clusters via Cloud Connected
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**
Elastic Inference Service (EIS) is now available to self-managed Elasticsearch deployments through Cloud Connect. EIS provides access to Elastic-managed LLM, vector generation, and rerank models running on fast, GPU-based infrastructure. It powers advanced capabilities such as RAG, semantic search, and the AI Assistants in Elastic’s Search, Observability, and Security solutions.

This release is designed for enterprise administrators, developers, and data teams running Elasticsearch on their own infrastructure who want to use high-performance, managed AI models without provisioning GPU hardware or managing complex third-party ML stacks. Through Cloud Connect, self-managed clusters connect securely to Elastic Cloud, automatically creating inference endpoints that integrate directly into existing workflows.

**Value proposition**
Self-managed Elasticsearch users can now run advanced AI-powered features with the same speed, scalability, and ease of use as Elastic Cloud customers. EIS removes the need to deploy and maintain GPU-accelerated ML nodes locally, reducing infrastructure costs and complexity. It offers predictable, per-token pricing and scales seamlessly from prototype to production.

By enabling EIS through Cloud Connect, organizations gain unified visibility and governance for connected clusters. Inference endpoints are automatically provisioned, enabling immediate use of vector search, semantic search, and AI Assistants with Elastic’s full suite of managed models.

Blog: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/cloud-connect-elastic-inference-service

Title: Serverless monitoring with AutoOps - Indexing Tier
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**
AutoOps for Elastic Cloud Serverless provides built-in views that show how project performance impacts compute and storage usage. The Search Tier view and Search AI Lake view help users understand how search activity, ingest, and retention affect VCUs and storage costs.

The new Indexing Tier view adds visibility into how indexing performance influences compute usage. It helps Serverless users managing high-volume or variable ingest workloads see how data ingestion and indexing behavior drive ingest VCU consumption and overall efficiency.

**Value proposition**
The Indexing Tier view connects ingest performance metrics with compute billing dimensions to show how indexing load and throughput impact VCU usage. It helps users identify scaling patterns, spot inefficiencies, and fine-tune pipelines to optimize performance and control costs.

Together with the Search Tier and Search AI Lake views, AutoOps enables Serverless users to track key billing dimensions, understand what drives consumption, and run cost-efficient, well-optimized projects.

Title: Serverless monitoring with AutoOps - Search AI lake and Search Tier
Description:
**What the feature is and who it’s for**
AutoOps for Elastic Cloud Serverless provides visibility into how project performance impacts compute and storage usage. Enabled automatically in supported regions, it offers curated dashboards, project-level metrics, and insight into key billing dimensions.

Elastic Cloud Serverless automatically manages provisioning, monitoring, and autoscaling, with billing based on actual resource usage. AutoOps helps users understand why consumption changes over time, how performance influences costs, and how to adjust workloads for better efficiency and cost control.

**Value proposition**
AutoOps gives Serverless users a clear view of how search, indexing, and machine learning workloads translate into resource consumption and costs. It connects performance insights with billing dimensions such as VCUs, ingest rate, and storage retention - making it easy to see how activity impacts compute and storage usage.

Available today, the Search Tier view shows how search activity and performance drive VCU consumption, while the Search AI Lake view summarizes ingest and retention patterns that influence storage costs. With this visibility, teams can identify inefficiencies, prevent unnecessary scaling, and forecast costs more accurately - helping them run efficient, cost-effective Serverless projects.

Title: Dashboard usage analytics in Kibana
Description:
**What the feature is** 

Dashboard usage analytics in Kibana

**Value proposition**

Learn how often your dashboards are being used--and by who to help better enable your end users.

Title: PromQL support in ES|QL
Description:
**What the feature is**

Enhanced support and tooling within the ES|QL editor to enable the construction of advanced time-series analysis queries, achieving functional parity with sophisticated metric query languages, including PromQL. This focuses on making complex calculations, like rates over time and pipelined aggregations, seamless and discoverable within the editor.

**Value proposition**

This feature targets DevOps engineers, SREs, and platform teams who perform high-fidelity metric analysis. Currently, performing complex time-series queries (like calculating rates or using variable windows) can be cumbersome or unsupported, often forcing users to rely on external, dedicated monitoring tools like Prometheus. This work integrates advanced time-series functions and PromQL concepts directly into the ES|QL editor experience, ensuring that users are guided by autocompletion and robust syntax support. The result is a unified and efficient editor where complex log and metric analysis can be performed without friction or context-switching.

Title: Create dashboards with natural language in chat

Create dashboards with natural language in chat

**Value proposition**
Users will be able to explore their data by asking the chat questions in natural language. The chat can leverage dashboards and visualizations as inputs for the reasoning agent as well as outputs when they are the most effective response, dramatically reducing the time-to-insights and eliminating the need for users to build them manually.

Title: AutoOps for air-gapped environments
Description:
**What is the feature and who it is for?**
AutoOps for air-gapped environments is an advanced monitoring, diagnostics, and optimization solution built for administrators running the Elastic Stack in secure, isolated environments, including Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes (ECK), Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE), or bare-metal installations. It is designed specifically for organizations with strict regulatory or security requirements, such as large-scale federal, government, and banking institutions who cannot send metrics to Elastic Cloud. The solution is deployed entirely within the customer's own environment, ensuring all analysis and metrics are performed and stored locally.

**Value proposition**
This new capability enhances AutoOps to support isolated environments, a capability that up until now was only available for Elastic Cloud Hosted or via Cloud Connected that require sending metrics to the cloud. This provides access to advanced, actionable insights within a secure, disconnected environment. Unlike other tools that only provide metrics, AutoOps correlates data to deliver insights, highlight potential causes for issues, and offer clear recommendations. This enables technical teams to perform guided troubleshooting, optimize resource utilization, and identify misconfigurations, ultimately reducing the time and expert resources required to manage large-scale Elastic deployments. All analysis is performed locally, ensuring no customer data leaves the secure network.

Title: Search Analytics Logs
Description:
**What the feature is and who is it for**
The new Search Analytics Logs capability is designed for administrators and search managers who need deeper visibility into the performance, usage, and sources of search queries within their Elasticsearch environments. This feature provides comprehensive logging of search queries, including both DSL and ES|QL types. Administrators can now monitor historical query performance, latency, as well as trace the origin of each query, whether from Kibana dashboards, background tasks, or remote clusters.

**Value proposition**
With Search Analytics Logs, organizations gain actionable insights to optimize search experiences. By surfacing Elasticsearch queries along with query times, and the sources of queries, administrators can quickly identify performance bottlenecks, inefficient queries, and slow remote clusters. This enables proactive troubleshooting, more efficient dashboard and rule design, and improved user education. The enhanced visibility and analytics empower teams to deliver faster, more reliable search experiences.

Title: Terraform Elasticstack - Security rules, CCS API Keys, Synthetics
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for:**
Recent improvements to the Elastic Stack and Elastic Cloud Terraform providers introduce advanced Infrastructure-as-Code capabilities for the latest stack and cloud features. These enhancements give administrators increased control and flexibility when managing Elastic environments with Terraform.

**Value proposition:**
The latest additions to the Terraform providers allow stack administrators to define Security detection rules and exceptions, Anomaly Detection Jobs, Synthetic APIs

Title: Search Management Dashboard in AutoOps
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for:**
The Search Management Dashboard is designed for administrators who need greater visibility and control over queries running in their Elasticsearch clusters. It provides a centralized interface that highlights long-running queries, making it easier for admins to identify and manage queries that could impact cluster performance. Currently, these capabilities are available in low-level tasks API. The new dashboard makes it simpler and more accessible to monitor and manage running queries.

**Value Proposition**
The Dashboard empowers administrators to quickly troubleshoot and resolve search bottlenecks, by offering a comprehensive view of all queries running in the cluster. Admins are presented with long-running queries that have been detected, and each query include a detailed information on the user who ran the query, and the origin (dashboard, alert rule etc). Administrators can then gain insights and act upon (e.g. cancel) them directly from the dashboard. Additionally AutoOps enrich each query with more information on potential reasons for the increase latency, and suggest query optimisations.

Title: Search Management Dashboard in Kibana
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for:**
Administrators often face challenges in identifying and managing queries that take longer to execute and can impact cluster performance. Additionally it is hard to track the source of those queries and who submitted them. Currently, locating these queries and acting upon them requires correlating multiple sources including the tasks API and query logs.

**Expected outcome**
The Search Management Dashboard is designed for these admins. It provides a centralized interface in Kibana that highlights long-running queries, making it easier for admins to identify and manage queries that could impact cluster performance. Currently, these capabilities are available in low-level tasks API. The new dashboard makes it simpler and more accessible to monitor and manage running queries.
Admins should be able to list running queries and see key details about each, like how long they've been running and who started them. They should be able to easily cancel a query from this list. This will give our admin users the tools they need to maintain optimal cluster health, peak search performance and quickly identify and resolve query inefficiencies.

Title: Lovable, Relevant Service Map
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for**
An improved service dependency visualization system designed for platform teams and architects who need to understand and monitor complex service relationships in large environments.

**Value proposition**
Provide efficient visualization and navigation of service dependencies for large environments, with support for embedding service maps in custom dashboards. Enable clear understanding of service relationships and their impact on system health.

**Expected outcome / behaviors**
- Improved usability for large service maps
- Clear service dependency visualization
- Basic service health indicators

**Key user stories**
- As an architect, I want to navigate complex service dependencies efficiently
- As a platform owner, I want to visualize large service environments

Title: SLO-Health at a Glance for APM
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for**
View the state of APM SLOs directly in your service inventory and service views so investigators can quickly understand which services are degraded at glance. 

**Value proposition**
During an investigation, understanding which services have SLOs which need attention can help identify problematic dependencies faster and restore service health.

Investigators will be able to spot which Services have unhealthy SLOs at a glance so they can prioritise their time during an investigation better.

**Expected outcome / behaviours**
- Understand service health at a glance in the service inventory/views 
- Prioritise investigations by focusing on what is healthy/unhealthy
- Create APM SLOs mor easily directly from the Service Inventory/views

**Key user stories**
- An an SRE, I want to understand which services are unhealthy so I can better prioritise my investigations 
- As a developer, I want to find the APM SLOs for my service in one place so I can get a wholistic view of my service in one place
- As a team lead, I want to create the right SLOs for my service directly from the Service Inventory/Views

Title: Trace Investigation in Discover
Description:
**What the feature is and who it's for**
A comprehensive trace search and analysis capability in Discover designed for developers, SREs, and DevOps engineers who need to investigate traces alongside other telemetry data using familiar Discover workflows.

**Value proposition**
Enable users to search and analyze traces directly in Discover using ESQL, reducing context switching between APM UI and Discover. Users can leverage familiar Discover capabilities for trace analysis while maintaining the ability to correlate with other telemetry data.

Title: Canvas layout options in Dashboards

Canvas layout options in Dashboards

Create pixel perfect fixed dashboard layouts that always looks the exact same when viewed and is optimal for large displays. Enable custom rich information displays that integrate internal business process diagrams and data from Elasticsearch.

Title: Customize the solution navigation in Kibana
Description:
**What the feature is**
Customize the solution navigation in Kibana allows users to re-order or hide menu items from the left-hand solution navigation on Serverless or when solution views are enabled in ECH / on-prem.

**Value Proposition**
This feature is designed for users who need to quickly access the menu items they use most. Currently, the solution navigation can be cluttered with many applications that are irrelevant to a user's specific role, making it hard to find or discover applications they care about. By hiding unused items and placing preferred applications at the top, users can speed up their workflow and focus only on the relevant parts of the Kibana interface. 

**Expected Outcome**
- A mechanism (e.g., a setting, modal, or side panel) will be introduced to allow users to configure their solution navigation.
- Hidden items will remain accessible via other means, such as the main search bar in Kibana.

**Key User Stories / Use Cases**
User Story: "As a Security Analyst, I only ever use Discover, Dashboards, and Alerts. I want to hide all other menu items (like Fleet, Maps, and Canvas) and place these applications at the very top of my navigation so I can jump straight to my core workflow every day."

User Story: "As a Developer who monitors my application with APM, I want to move the APM menu item right below Discover and hide SLOs, Synthetics, and Streams to create a cleaner workspace that only shows my performance monitoring tools."

Title: Serverless Cross Project Search: Users can control which linked projects to include in their Cross-project search query using user-friendly attributes
Description: To improve query performance and relevance, users need an intuitive way to filter which linked projects are included in a search, rather than relying on cryptic identifiers. CPS introduces project routing based on business-friendly metadata tags defined by default (like the project region or cloud provider), or defined by the user (like env:prod or `team:security). This scope is managed via a Kibana component that can be set at various levels, including at the dashboard or panel level.

Title: More flexible CCS version compatibility between clusters
Description:
Customers with multiple clusters connected together via CCS struggle with planning stack upgrades The current version compatibility model requires customers to upgrade the local cluster last. As a result, the central/local cluster might end up remaining on an older, potentially vulnerable version of the stack because remotes are not upgraded yet.

Customers solve this today by maintaining a dedicated cluster for cross-cluster search. Keeping this cluster on the earliest version needed to search the other clusters. For example, if you have 7.17 and 8.x clusters, you can maintain a dedicated 7.17 cluster to use as the local cluster for cross-cluster search. Or they keep each cluster no more than one minor version apart. This lets them use any cluster as the local cluster when running a cross-cluster search.

We would like to allow remote versions to diverge by more than v-1

Title: Admins have insights about CCS queries health and performance via dashboard and alerts
Description:
Customers with multiple remote clusters, prevalent in enterprise, government, and Security Solution users, using CCS need to offer a reliable and performant search/dashboard service to their users. To achieve that, they need visibility into CCS queries' health and performance.

Today, some customers make their own dashboards and find crafty solutions to gather some data on the CCS queries or remote cluster health. We know of one that has a scheduled python script and a watcher that runs sample queries against the remotes so they have status data to show in a CCS Stability dashboard they have created.

Title: "Tailing" in Discover
Description:
**What the feature is** 

"Tailing" in Discover: An optional Tail Mode (Live Streaming) configuration in the Discover table that allows users to continuously append and view new documents in near real-time, similar to watching a live stream of logs.

**Value proposition**:

This feature is designed for users who require real-time monitoring of logs and metrics. Currently, monitoring a live stream of data requires constantly hitting refresh or using the auto-refresh feature, which inefficiently reloads the entire view, disrupting scrolling and reading flow. Tail Mode solves this by providing a lightweight, incremental update mechanism that only appends new documents to the bottom of the table, preserving your context and enabling continuous, non-disruptive, real-time data analysis.

**Expected outcome**:

- Enable a Tail Mode toggle in the table configuration menu to start live streaming.
- When active, the table will automatically append only the newest documents at a regular interval (defaulting to 10 seconds). 
- The view will auto-scroll to the bottom to show the latest documents, but will pause updates if you scroll up to inspect older data.
- A visual indicator will notify you of "X new documents" when auto-scrolling is paused.
- This feature only works on relative time ranges that end at "now."

Title: CCS support in all new ES|QL features and functions: INLINE STATS, FORK, RERANK, COMPLETION
Description: The new ES|QL features INLINE STATS, FORK, RERANK, and COMPLETION do not support Cross-cluster queries. This is limiting their use by customers relying on CCS for all of their queries. All ES|QL features and functions must support CCS, so these features cannot go GA without CCS support.

Title: Streamstats in ES|QL: running statistics over time windows
Description:
**Streamstats in ES|QL provide running statistics over time windows**

**Value Proposition**

Add dynamic statistical calculations to each individual event as it is processed, based on preceding events or specific groupings. This command allows you to enrich your data with running totals, averages, and counts without altering the event structure, providing immediate context for trend analysis, performance monitoring, and anomaly detection.

**Expected Outcome**

Enriched Event Data: Each event can be augmented with statistics derived from a window of prior events, providing immediate context for its values.
Running Calculations: Users will be able to compute running sums, counts, averages, and other aggregate measures per event, over a specified window or group.
Temporal Trend Identification: Observe how metrics evolve over time for individual entities or across event sequences, assisting in identifying patterns or deviations.
Contextual Monitoring: Add event-specific statistics that aid in monitoring system behavior, user activity, or process performance by showing how current events relate to recent history.
Support for Anomaly Detection: Provide additional data points on each event, such as a rolling average or standard deviation, which can be used to identify unusual occurrences.
Preservation of Event Detail: Perform statistical analysis without aggregating away the original individual events, allowing for deeper investigation.

Title: Lookup IP database information in ES|QL queries
Description:
**What the feature is**
Dynamic Geographical Enrichment of IP Addresses at Query Time

**Value Proposition**

Instantly add geographical details (such as country, city, and coordinates) to IP addresses directly within your search queries. This command provides immediate geographical context for network activity and enables location-based analysis and visualization on demand, offering greater flexibility and reducing the need for upfront data modification compared to ingest-time processing. Specifically, users want to extract an IP address that was not parsed at ingest time and apply an ip-to-geo lookup using the internal MMDB databases. This feature would enhance their security analytics capabilities by allowing dynamic GEO data enrichment during search.

**Expected Outcome**
Flexible On-Demand Enrichment: Unlike geoip or IP_Location ingest pipeline processors that enrich data at indexing, this command allows users to dynamically add geographical information to IP addresses during a query. This means enrichment can be applied selectively when needed, without pre-processing all data.
Reduced Ingest Overhead: Data does not need to be enriched with geo-location fields at ingest if it's not always required, preserving storage space and reducing indexing time.
Enhanced Ad-hoc Analysis: Analysts can quickly add location context to any IP address in their results during an investigation, even for data that was not originally enriched at ingest, supporting dynamic threat hunting and incident response.
Always Current Geo-Data: Queries can automatically use the latest available geo-IP database, ensuring that location information is as accurate and up-to-date as possible without requiring re-indexing of historical data.
Improved Security Analysis: Gain a geographical dimension for identifying suspicious logins, unusual traffic patterns, or potential security breaches across different regions.
Location-Based Reporting and Visualization: Easily create maps, regional breakdowns, and reports that show the geographical distribution of your data, all based on freshly enriched query results.

**Optional: Key user stories / use cases**

Title: Dedup command: Filter out or dedup duplicate data in ES|QL queries
Description:
**Dedup command: Filter out or dedup duplicate data in ES|QL queries**

**Value proposition**

Sometimes the processing stages of a query can result in duplicate data. Users want to remove the events that contain an identical combination of values for the fields that they specify. This enables more precise and relevant data results by identifying and removing duplicate events or documents according to your chosen criteria. Clearer Analysis: Data becomes easier to interpret, as redundant information is removed, allowing a focus on distinct events.
Simplified Data Preparation: Users will spend less effort on manual or complex methods to filter out duplicate records, making data ready for use more quickly.
